subject.title: unsafe plugin path error after onboarding

question: Should release-mode installs fix this by changing the OpenClaw install location/package-manager policy, by pinning a known-good release, or by changing trusted plugin roots while preserving unsafe manifest path validation?
rationale: The observed failure is in first-run onboarding, but the repair crosses plugin path validation and installer release policy, so automation should not pick a trust-boundary change without maintainer intent.

options.title: Preserve validation and fix installer policy
options.body: Make release installs place bundled manifests where OpenClaw already trusts them, or install a maintainer-approved known-good release, with fresh onboarding proof.

options.title: Use version pinning as the first mitigation
options.body: Land or revise the open pinning work so operators can avoid known-bad OpenClaw releases, while separately deciding the default latest path.

options.title: Route to upstream package trust policy
options.body: Keep this installer unchanged until OpenClaw core defines how pnpm global package manifests should be trusted or rejected.

recommendation.title: Preserve validation and fix installer policy
recommendation.body: Make release installs place bundled manifests where OpenClaw already trusts them, or install a maintainer-approved known-good release, with fresh onboarding proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Alec Olson introduced the current OpenClaw release package path and is the strongest history signal for the installer-side policy decision.
